tagline: Farmland, marsh islands and a bay whose tides follow the wind
intro: Low-speed, two-lane Sandbridge Road leads to a coastal community between the Atlantic Ocean and Back Bay. The Atlantic lies east of Sandbridge; Back Bay lies west. Across the bay, Pungo farmland occupies the western side.

Sandbridge once had another connection: residents with permits could drive through the neighboring Dam Neck naval installation. That back gate closed for security after September 11. Sandbridge Road also forms part of Virginia Beach’s Green Line, the boundary for urban growth.

The refuge’s visitor contact center is reached from Sandbridge by Sandpiper Road. Inland, Pungo’s center is the intersection of Princess Anne and Indian River roads. Mill Landing provides public boat access to Back Bay, where wind drives the tides. The bay connects with the Atlantic only through Oregon Inlet, more than 60 miles south.

moments.title: Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Freshwater marshes and Atlantic beaches share this refuge on the Currituck Banks Peninsula. The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service established it in 1938 to protect wildlife habitat, particularly for migrating and wintering waterfowl. Its protected landscape included five miles of open water and marsh and 4½ miles of dunes and Atlantic beachfront. Most refuge marshland lies on islands in Back Bay; large impoundments provide habitat for wintering wildfowl. Migrating and wintering birds protected here include tundra swans, black ducks and redheads, along with shorebirds, herons and ospreys. The refuge adjoins False Cape State Park to the south.
moments.notice: Look for dunes, maritime forest and freshwater marshes within the barrier-island landscape.

moments.title: Pungo
moments.text: Pungo’s center has one stoplight, at Princess Anne and Indian River roads. Farmland surrounds this rural community in southern Virginia Beach. It belonged to Princess Anne County until 1963, when the whole county became part of Virginia Beach. Pungo then became one of the new city’s seven original boroughs. The community lies south of Sandbridge Road and the city’s Green Line, a boundary intended to keep Pungo rural while neighborhoods to its north developed. The Military Aviation Museum at Virginia Beach Airport houses a collection of vintage warbirds, another part of this rural community’s present identity.

moments.title: Mill Landing
moments.text: Mill Landing is a public launch on a bay whose tides respond to wind rather than the moon. Back Bay’s shallow fresh and mildly brackish water contains marsh islands and underwater grass beds. Its bass fishery collapsed in the mid-1980s under fishing pressure and damage from development. Sediment and algae blocked the light reaching underwater grasses, and their meadows died. DWR biologist Chad Boyce links improving bay health to land conservation and better environmental practices on farms and developed land. In 2009, DWR stocked 70,000 surplus largemouth bass fingerlings here; monitoring their survival supported a larger investment in stocking.
